questions.q: A paralegal misses a filing deadline, resulting in their client's claim being dismissed. The client threatens to sue the paralegal for malpractice. What must the paralegal do regarding their insurance provider?
options: The paralegal must wait until an actual lawsuit is filed against them before contacting their insurer.
The paralegal must immediately notify their professional liability insurer about the potential claim.
The paralegal must attempt to settle with the client using personal funds before involving the insurer.
The paralegal must cancel their insurance policy immediately.
questions.explain: Rule 3.01 (Competence and Errors) requires a paralegal to give prompt notice of any circumstance that may give rise to a claim to their professional liability insurer (and to the client). Attempting to secretly settle a malpractice claim or waiting until a lawsuit is formally filed can void coverage and violates LSO rules.
